## About

I'm a Ph.D. candidate in Biological Sciences (minor: Statistics) at the
University of Nebraska–Lincoln, defending in August 2026. My work sits at
the intersection of plant demography, remote sensing, and global change
biology — I ask how long-term environmental stress and disturbance shape
plant population dynamics, and how modern spatial data can scale that
understanding beyond the plot level.

My dissertation examines lagged water-stress effects and insect herbivory
on native perennial thistles (*Cirsium undulatum*) using more than 20 years
of field data. I'm currently expanding into UAV-based multispectral remote
sensing, building an R pipeline to link vegetation indices and spectral
texture to grassland community resilience.

I'm on the job market for postdoctoral and research positions in
quantitative ecology, spatial ecology, and data science.

## Research interests

- Long-term plant population and community demography
- Global change effects on grassland resilience
- Multispectral / UAV remote sensing for ecological monitoring
- Statistical and machine learning methods for ecological inference
  (GLMMs, GAMs, IPMs, Random Forest, XGBoost)

## Currently

Working on the **DRAGNet grassland resilience project**, combining UAV
multispectral imagery with field vegetation data across five experimental
treatments (2024–2025) to quantify community-level resilience to disturbance.
